paragraphs.source_en: Tadachika, exiled to Kyushu, was certainly pitiable, yet he had also once plunged Ieyasu into unbearable anxiety—at the time Ieyasu could neither return to Sunpu nor go to Edo Castle, and could only make brief stops at Nakahara, Kosugi, and other places. Even now, Ieyasu felt a chill in his breast whenever he recalled it.

paragraphs.source_en: Besides Hon'ami Kōetsu, there were three men in the Kyoto–Osaka region who revered Ieyasu from the heart and voluntarily gathered information for him. One was Kobori Enshū in Fushimi, another Ishikawa Jōzan at the Yamazaki gateway, and the third Sōkun at the port of Sakai. paragraphs.source_en: Rōnin from every province were streaming without cease into the Kyoto and Osaka region.
